Hey infra/ML — need a short ops guideline: when to prefer vendor-provided attention kernels vs FlashAttention v3 or Triton for production routing. Keep it 1-paragraph + bullet rules.

Action items:
- lee: PR with routing + canary (ETA EOD)
- priya: full bench matrix (seq=128/512/1024/2048, batch=1/4/8, q4/q8) across A100/H100 (ETA 48h)
- sam/anya: run token-level quality evals on vendor q4_hf and report diffs (ASAP)

Thanks all :thumbsup:
sam:
Quick summary from recent benches (H100 L40 & A100 80GB, Mistral-7B-instruct, q4_hf):

```
seq=128, batch=1: Flashv3 p50=8.7ms p99=18.9ms, vendor p50=8.1ms p99=20.2ms
seq=512, batch=4: Flashv3 p50=23ms p99=58ms, vendor p50=19.5ms p99=53ms
seq=2048, batch=8: Flashv3 p50=95ms p99=220ms, vendor p50=72ms p99=190ms
throughput (tokens/s): Flashv3 7.3k, vendor 9.6k
cpu overhead (kernel launches): vendor lower on A100
```

Add a mandatory quality eval for vendor kernels on quantized configs  run: `evals/compare_token_level.py --model Mistral-7B --q q4_hf --kernels vendor,flashv3`
anya:
TL;DR vendor tends to beat Flashv3 at long context and high-throughput workloads; Flashv3 often matches or beats vendor on tiny-latency single-token calls on some driver/kernel combos.

Note about tokenization/byte-level diffs: vendor libs have sometimes used fused token remapping which changed tie-breaks for subword scores. Manual spot-check on 50 prompts before promoting.
lee:
Ops/caveat: vendor binaries are opaque and occasionally introduce regressions (safety model mispredictions once). Must canary and keep a fast rollback path. Also vendor updates are not guaranteed to be ABI-stable across driver updates.

I'll open a small PR to runtime routing with thresholds + a bench script (tools/bench_kernel_compare.py) and add the canary template. ETA: EOD tomorrow.
priya:
Proposed condensed decision guide to add to runtime kernel routing:
- Default: FlashAttention v3 for new model bring-ups on Hosted (better traceability + open-source fixes).
- Benchmark gate: if vendor shows >=20% throughput uplift OR >=15% p50 latency improvement on target HW (A100/H100) for the model+quant config, promote to dedicated canary.
- Sequence rule: prefer vendor for seq_len >= 1024 and batch >= 4 unless quality eval fails.
- Quantization rule: for q4/q4_hf prefer Flashv3 unless vendor reduces CPU overhead or shows >10% token throughput improvement.
- Fallback rule: auto-fallback to Flashv3 if production p99 (1h window) for vendor > Flashv3 p99 by 12% and error rate rises.
